stimulus_db: After replacing his old gas water heater with a new, pilotless, gas water heater that is rated as highly efficient, Jimmy’s gas bills increased.
stem_db: Each of the following, if true, contributes to an explanation of the increase mentioned above EXCEPT:

choices_db.A: The new water heater uses a smaller percentage of the gas used by Jimmy’s household than did the old one.
choices_db.B: Shortly after the new water heater was installed, Jimmy’s uncle came to live with him, doubling the size of the household.
choices_db.C: After having done his laundry at a laundromat, Jimmy bought and started using a gas dryer when he replaced his water heater.
choices_db.D: Jimmy’s utility company raised the rates for gas consumption following installation of the new water heater.
choices_db.E: Unusually cold weather following installation of the new water heater resulted in heavy gas usage.

steps.label: Apparent Paradox
steps.body: After replacing his old gas water heater with a new, pilotless, gas water heater that is rated as highly efficient, Jimmy’s gas bills increased.

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.body: More gas usage or higher gas rates would explain the increase in Jimmy’s gas bills.

notes.body: This deepens the paradox since it implies that Jimmy’s new water heater used less gas than before.
Doubling the household means more people using hot water and more gas used overall. More gas used would raise the bill even with an efficient heater, so B helps explain the increase.
Jimmy started using a gas dryer at the same time the water heater was replaced. That is a new source of gas use, which helps explain why the bill went up.
If the utility raised its rates, Jimmy pays more for each unit of gas. Jimmy's bill could rise even if the new heater uses less gas, so D helps explain the increase.
The unusually cold weather led to heavy gas usage. More gas burned for heat would raise the bill, whatever the water heater's efficiency, so E helps explain the increase.

known_problem: EXCEPT Paradox: B-E share one pasted sentence; no prediction of the two routes (more usage, higher rates).
